figures.caption: Fig. 1. A schematic of synaptic transmission and a sample trajectory of the membrane potential from the associated synaptic model. A: Synaptic vesicles docked at docking sites at the active zone of the excitatory and inhibitory presynaptic axon terminals fuse with the membrane and release their neurotransmitter content into the synaptic cleft. These neurotransmitters bind to receptors on the postsynaptic neuron, opening channels that allow ions to flow across the cell and alter its membrane potential. B: A simulated trajectory of the postsynaptic neuron’s membrane potential as modeled in equations (1) and (2). The membrane potential (solid blue line) depolarizes upon the arrival of excitatory presynaptic action potentials (red dashed line), which arrive via a Poisson process with rate fe. Inhibitory presynaptic APs (dashed blue line) arrive via a Poisson process with rate fi. The excitatory and inhibitory QC is modeled as binomial random variables with means ⟨be⟩ = ⟨bi⟩ = 1 and noise CV 2 be = CV 2 bi = 0.95, respectively. Between presynaptic APs, the membrane potential returns to a resting potential, here 0, with time constant τv . Once the membrane potential exceeds a threshold potential vth (black line), the postsynaptic neuron fires an action potential (red circles). The inter-spike interval (ISI) is the time period between successive postsynaptic APs. Parameters: fe = 100 Hz, fi = 100 Hz, τv = 10 ms, vth = 20 mV , ce = ci = 20 mV, vr = 0 mV .

Fig. 2. The mean postsynaptic firing frequency and inter-spike interval (ISI) noise profile vary with the membrane time constant. A: Trajectories of the membrane and threshold potential in (1) and (2) as a function of time when τv = ∞. The membrane potential (blue line) increases if the arriving presynaptic AP is excitatory and decreases if the arriving presynaptic AP is inhibitory. Upon being driven to the threshold potential vth (black line), the postsynaptic neuron fires an AP (red dot) and resets to a resting potential vr = 0 mV . B: Theoretical predictions of the mean postsynaptic firing frequency as a function of the excitatory and inhibitory input frequency based on equation (9). C: Simulations of the mean postsynaptic firing frequency as a function of the excitatory and inhibitory input frequency in (1) and (2). D: Simulations of the ISI noise for a pure integrator as a function of the excitatory and inhibitory input frequency. The excitatory and inhibitory QC for each of these plots is modeled as binomial distributions with means ⟨be⟩ = 1 and noise CV 2 be = 0.95. Parameters: τv = 100 ms, τth = 100 ms, vb = 20 mV , vmin = −50 mV , vI = 10 mV , aT = 0.8 mV , ce = ci = 2 mV, vr = 0 mV .

Fig. 3. The inter-spike interval (ISI) noise is larger in neurons with a depolarizing adaptive threshold than those with a fixed threshold. A: The steady state threshold potential as a function of the membrane potential as described in equation (13). B: Trajectories of the depolarizing adaptive threshold and membrane potential as a function of time. The membrane potential (blue line) evolves via (1) and (2) while the threshold potential (black line) evolves via (12) and (13). In these simulations, the postsynaptic neuron only receives excitation (fi = 0). Once the membrane potential is driven to the threshold potential, the postsynaptic neuron fires an AP (red dot). The inter-spike interval (ISI) is the time interval between successive postsynaptic APs. C: A comparison of the mean postsynaptic firing frequency as a function of the excitatory input frequency for both a fixed threshold and the depolarizing adaptive threshold. D: The ISI noise as a function of the excitatory input frequency for both a fixed threshold and a depolarizing adaptive threshold model. For each value of fe, the mean postsynaptic firing frequencies of the two models were matched by incrementally adjusting the adaptive threshold parameter vb until the difference between the mean postsynaptic firing frequencies was within a 10 µHz difference. The excitatory and inhibitory QC for each of these plots is modeled as binomial distributions with means ⟨be⟩ = 1 and noise CV 2 be = 0.95. Parameters: τv = 100 ms, τth = 100 ms, vb = 20 mV , vmin = −50 mV , vI = 10 mV , aT = 0.8 mV, ce = 2 mV, vr = 0 mV .

Fig. 4. The mean postsynaptic firing frequency of a neuron with a depolarizing adaptive threshold increases with excitatory input frequency. A: The mean postsynaptic firing frequency as a function of the excitatory and inhibitory input frequency. B: The ISI noise as a function of the excitatory and inhibitory input frequency. The curved black line represents the excitatory-inhibitory input frequency space where noise, defined by CV 2 T , is 1. The space contained within the curved line has CV 2 T > 1 and CV 2 T < 1 outside of this curved line. C: The mean postsynaptic firing frequency as a function of the threshold and membrane time constants. The black line shows the mean postsynaptic firing frequency for τth = τv . Above and below the black line shows the mean postsynaptic firing frequency for τth > τv , and τth < τv , respectively. D: The ISI noise as a function of the threshold and membrane time constants. The excitatory and inhibitory QC for each of these plots is modeled as binomial distributions with means ⟨be⟩ = 1 and noise CV 2 be = 0.95. Parameters: τv = 100 ms, τth = 100 ms, vb = 20 mV , vmin = −50 mV , vI = 10 mV , aT = 0.8 mV, ce = 2 mV, vr = 0 mV .

Fig. 6. The mean postsynaptic firing rate of a neuron with a hyperpolarizing adaptive threshold is maximized at intermediate membrane and threshold time constants. A: The mean postsynaptic firing frequency as a function of the excitatory and inhibitory input frequency. The white line shows the mean postsynaptic firing frequency for fe = 20 Hz, and the white circle on the white line represents the maximum postsynaptic firing frequency occurring at fi = 265 Hz. B: The ISI noise as a function of the excitatory and inhibitory input frequency. The black line represents the parameter space of fe and fi where CV 2 T = 1. In the space to the left of the black line CV 2 T < 1, and to the right of the black line CV 2 T > 1. C: The mean postsynaptic firing frequency as a function of the threshold and membrane time constant. The mean postsynaptic firing frequency is maximized at intermediate values of the time constants. D: The ISI noise as a function of the threshold and membrane time constants. In A-D, the excitatory and inhibitory QC are modeled as a binomial distribution with means ⟨be⟩ = ⟨bi⟩ = 1 and noise CV 2 be = CV 2 bi = 0.95. Parameters: τv = 10 ms, τth = 20 ms, vb = 20 mV , v1 = −50 mV , vlow = −40 mV , ci = 2 mV, ce = 2 mV, vr = 0 mV .
